home.getText: AI tarot readings for your own cards, on iPhone and Android.

free.a: Yes, to start. You get a free Card of the Day and free AI readings with up to three cards every day once you sign in. Premium adds more.

account.a: Only for AI readings. You can draw cards and look up meanings without one. For AI readings, sign in with Google or Apple, so there is no new password to create.

deck.q: Do I need my own tarot deck?
deck.a: No. You can scan your own Rider-Waite-Smith deck with the camera, or draw cards on screen from the full 78-card deck.

photo.q: Is the photo of my cards uploaded?
photo.a: No. Cards are recognised on your phone and the photo is never saved or sent. Only the card names and your question are used to write the reading.

how.q: How does the AI tarot reading work?
how.a: ShenTarot picks a spread for your question, then writes a reading from the cards you drew, their positions and whether they are upright or reversed. You can ask a follow-up about it.

predict.a: ShenTarot is for entertainment and self-reflection. Readings help you think through a question; they are not predictions or professional advice.

yesNo.title: Yes or No tarot: free three-card reading · ShenTarot
yesNo.description: Ask a yes or no question and draw three tarot cards. Upright cards lean yes, reversed lean no, and the middle card counts double. Free, in your browser.
yesNo.lead: Hold a clear yes or no question in mind and draw three cards. Upright cards lean yes, reversed cards lean no, and the middle card counts double. Each card comes up reversed half the time, so neither answer is favoured.
yesNo.howTitle: How to ask a good yes or no question
yesNo.how1: Ask about one thing, and about something you can act on: "Should I apply for the design job?" works better than "Will my life get better?"
yesNo.how2: Ask once. Drawing again for the same question just adds noise.
yesNo.how3: Read the three meanings, not only the lean. They show what could tip the answer the other way.
yesNo.note: For entertainment and self-reflection. For health, money or legal questions, talk to a professional. See also the {link}.

daily.description: Draw your tarot card of the day, with its meaning and a question to reflect on. Your card stays the same until tomorrow. Free, in your browser.
daily.lead: Take a breath, think about the day ahead and draw one card. Read its meaning in the morning, and come back to the question tonight. Your card stays the same until tomorrow.

weekly.lead: Seven cards, one for each day from Monday to Sunday. Draw at the start of the week, then come back each day to read that day's card. Shuffled in your browser.

pairing.majorTheme: {major} sets the theme; {minor} shows where it plays out day to day.

pairing.twoSameRank: Two {rank}: two people, or two sides of you, acting in a similar way.

pairing.bothReversed: Both reversed: the energy of both cards is blocked, delayed or turned inward. Ask what is holding it back.
pairing.oneReversed: {name} is reversed: one part flows while the other is blocked or turned inward.

rel.same: share an element, so they strengthen each other

rel.contrary: have opposite elements, so they weaken each other

pairing.muchWeak: {name} is much weakened: both neighbours oppose it. Read it lightly, as a smaller influence.
pairing.mixed: {name} is mixed: one neighbour supports it and one opposes it.
pairing.someWeak: {name} is somewhat weakened by one opposing neighbour.
pairing.strong: {name} is strengthened: both neighbours support it. Read it as a strong influence.
pairing.someStrong: {name} is somewhat strengthened by one supporting neighbour.
pairing.neither: {name} is neither helped nor hindered by its neighbours.
pairing.bridge: {l} and {r} oppose each other, but {m} gets on with both: it can bridge the two.

notFate: Themes you may grow into, not a fixed fate.

birth.title: Tarot birth card calculator: find your birth cards · ShenTarot
birth.description: Find your tarot birth cards and your card for this year from your birthday. Worked out in your browser; nothing is sent.
birth.lead: A traditional numerology method: add your birth month, day and year, then add the digits until you reach 22 or less. That number is a Major Arcana card (22 is The Fool). A two-digit result also gives the card for the sum of its digits. Worked out in your browser; nothing is sent.

life.title: Life path number calculator with its tarot card · ShenTarot
life.description: Work out your numerology life path number from your birthday, including master numbers 11, 22 and 33, and see the Major Arcana card that goes with it.
life.h1: Life path number and tarot card
life.lead: Add up every digit of your birth date and reduce it to one digit, keeping the master numbers 11, 22 and 33. Each number has a Major Arcana card. Worked out in your browser; nothing is sent.
life.note: Numbers 1 to 9 and 11 match the Major Arcana card with that number. 22 is The Fool, and 33 adds to 6, The Lovers. This is a different sum from the {link}, which adds the month, day and year as whole numbers.

year.title: Tarot year card calculator: your card for the year · ShenTarot
year.description: Find your personal tarot year card from your birthday, for this year or the next, with what it means and a question to carry through the year.
year.lead: Add your birth month and day to the year you want to look at, then reduce the total to a Major Arcana card. That card is a theme for your year. Worked out in your browser; nothing is sent.
year.how: Add your birth month, your birth day and the year, then add the digits of the total until it is 22 or less. 22 is The Fool. The card changes each year, so it is worth looking again at every birthday. Your {link} use your birth year instead and stay the same for life.
year.question: A question for the year: {q}

compat.title: Tarot love compatibility: compare two birth cards · ShenTarot
compat.description: Enter two birthdays to find each person's tarot birth card and see how the two cards and their elements get on. Free, and worked out in your browser.
compat.lead: Each birthday gives a Major Arcana birth card. Compare the two cards and their elements to see where you meet and where you may clash. Worked out in your browser; nothing is sent.
compat.how: Add the month, day and year of a birthday, then add the digits until the total is 22 or less. That number is the person's birth card (22 is The Fool). Then each card's element is compared the way readers compare cards in a spread: the same element strengthens, Fire and Water or Air and Earth pull against each other, and the other pairs support each other. Cards linked to a planet have no single element.
compat.note: For fun and reflection. No pair of cards decides whether a relationship works.
compat.sameCard: The same card: you may see yourself in each other, strengths and habits alike.

rel.same: Your cards share an element, so you understand each other easily. Watch for having the same blind spots.
rel.friendly: Your cards' elements support each other. You bring different things that fit together.
rel.contrary: Your cards' elements pull against each other. There is spark and friction; it works when you respect the difference.
rel.neutral: One of your cards is linked to a planet rather than an element, so it adapts to the other.

zodiac.lead: In the Golden Dawn tradition behind the Rider-Waite-Smith deck, every star sign has its own Major Arcana card, a ruling planet with a card of its own, and three numbered cards for the thirds of the sign.

comb.title: Tarot card combinations: read two cards together · ShenTarot
comb.description: Pick any two tarot cards, upright or reversed, and see how they read together: theme and detail, suits, numbers, court cards and elements. Free, in your browser.
comb.lead: Pick two cards from a reading, or draw two at random, and see what links them: which one sets the theme, what their suits, numbers and elements say, and a question from each card to reflect on.
comb.howTitle: How to read two cards together
how: Read each card on its own first, then ask how one changes the other. The second card often answers or qualifies the first.
A Major Arcana card carries more weight. When it sits next to a Minor Arcana card, the Major names the theme and the Minor shows how it shows up.
Try one sentence that holds both meanings. If it feels forced, look at the picture on each card for a detail they share.
comb.note: For entertainment and self-reflection. See also {elements} and {cards}.

elem.title: Elemental dignities in tarot: free checker · ShenTarot
elem.description: Check the elemental dignities of two or three tarot cards. See which cards strengthen or weaken each other by Fire, Water, Air and Earth. Free, in your browser.
elem.lead: A method from the Golden Dawn tradition, often used instead of reversals. Each card has an element, and cards next to each other strengthen or weaken one another. Pick a line of two or three cards to check them.
how: Wands are Fire, Cups are Water, Swords are Air and Pentacles are Earth.
take the element of their traditional zodiac sign or element. Cards linked to a planet have no single element here and count as neutral.
(Fire and Water, Air and Earth) weaken each other.
support each other. Some readers count Fire with Earth, and Air with Water, as neutral instead.
the middle card is judged by both neighbours. A card between two friends is strong; a card between two opposites is weak.
elem.note: Each card's element is listed on its {cards}. To read two cards together, try {comb}.
